title: India's Cricket Schedule, Squads and Draw for Asian Games 2026 in Japan
excerpt: Shreyas Iyer and Harmanpreet Kaur lead India's men's and women's teams at the Korogi Athletic Park in Aichi-Nagoya, with the women's tournament starting September 17 and men's on September 24.
body:
• India's women's cricket tournament runs September 17–22 and the men's from September 24 to October 3 at Korogi Athletic Park in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.
  • Shreyas Iyer captains the men's squad featuring Jasprit Bumrah and teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, with VVS Laxman coaching the side.
  • Harmanpreet Kaur leads the women's team, which opens against hosts Japan in the quarterfinals on September 17.
  • All matches carry full T20 International status — India enters both draws as the defending champion from Hangzhou 2023.

Tournament Format and Venues

Cricket returns to the Asian Games for the fourth time since its debut at Guangzhou 2010, with both tournaments contested in T20 International format at the Korogi Athletic Park in Nisshin, Aichi Prefecture. The women's competition kicks off on September 17 with quarterfinal matches, culminating in the final on September 22. The men's event follows from September 24 through October 3, according to Sporting News.

India enters both draws as the defending champion after sweeping gold at Hangzhou 2023. The men's tournament overlaps with India's home T20I series against the West Indies, forcing the BCCI to run two separate squads simultaneously — VVS Laxman will coach the Asian Games contingent while the main coaching setup stays with the West Indies series, according to Livemint.

Men's Squad: Iyer Leads, Bumrah and Sooryavanshi Headline

Shreyas Iyer takes the captaincy with Tilak Varma as vice-captain. The 15-member squad blends proven performers with emerging talent. Jasprit Bumrah, Arshdeep Singh, and Harshit Rana form a formidable pace attack, while Varun Chakaravarthy, Ravi Bishnoi, and Washington Sundar anchor the spin department. Sanju Samson and Ishan Kishan share wicketkeeping duties.

The standout inclusion is Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, the teenage batting sensation who scored a record 18-ball fifty in the first T20I against Zimbabwe in Harare. His selection signals the BCCI's long-term investment in the 17-year-old's development alongside senior players like Nitish Kumar Reddy and Shivam Dube.

Men's Draw: India Seeded Into Quarterfinals

Ten teams contest the men's event. India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, and Bangladesh are seeded directly into the quarterfinals, bypassing the preliminary round. The remaining six teams — Afghanistan, Japan, and Nepal in Group A; Hong Kong China, Malaysia, and Oman in Group B — play a round-robin phase, with the top two from each group advancing.

India's quarterfinal is scheduled for September 28 at 9:00 AM JST (5:30 AM IST), according to LatestLY. The draw places India and Pakistan on opposite sides of the bracket, meaning they can only meet in the final — a prospect that would electrify cricket fans worldwide.

Women's Squad and Path to Gold

Harmanpreet Kaur retains the captaincy with Smriti Mandhana as vice-captain. The squad features explosive opener Shafali Verma, who recently became the youngest player to reach 3,000 Women's T20I runs, alongside Jemimah Rodrigues, all-rounder Deepti Sharma, and wicketkeeper Richa Ghosh. Renuka Singh Thakur spearheads the pace attack, with Radha Yadav, Sree Charani, and Shreyanka Patil forming a deep spin contingent.

India's women open against hosts Japan in the quarterfinals on September 17. Bangladesh face China, Sri Lanka take on Malaysia, and Pakistan meet Thailand in the remaining last-eight encounters. The semifinals follow on September 20, with the final on September 22.

How to Watch

Sony Sports Network and Sony LIV have been confirmed as broadcast partners for the Asian Games cricket tournaments, according to LatestLY. The compact knockout format means high-stakes elimination cricket from the quarterfinals onward — no group-stage cushion for the seeded teams. With both squads locked in and the draw set, the countdown to Aichi-Nagoya is on.
